name: pi
notes: Paths verified against pi's own documentation (skills.md, configuration.md, prompt-templates.md, mcp.md). Skills are DECLARED AS A LINK rather than copied: pi documents ~/.agents/skills/ as a natively supported location, and sharing it by link gives pi the source's skills with no duplication and no drift to reconcile. The bridge CREATES that link (a symlink on POSIX, a junction on Windows) on the first adopt when it is missing, and recreates it if it was deleted. The rules document goes to ~/AGENTS.md rather than ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md because pi loads context files from both the agent directory and the working-directory chain, so a second copy under ~/.pi would make the model read the same rules twice. MACHINE-LOCAL GATE SCOPE: bridge/lib/gates.js merges ~/.config/agent-config-bridge/gate-policy.json (config only) when generating policy.json, so a machine can declare project_roots outside this public repository and cover non-git working directories without committing absolute paths here. scaffold it with `node scripts/bootstrap.js --yes --root <dev-root>`. NOTE: pi >= 1.4 has BUILT-IN MCP support and reads ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json (user level) plus .pi/mcp.json (project level); the older pi-mcp-adapter package and its ~/.pi/agent/mcp-adapter.json are no longer needed. NOTE ON MODEL METADATA: pi-smart-router keeps its own copy of every model's contextWindow in ~/.pi/agent/pi-router-catalog.json, and its merge is sticky (an existing value always wins), so a stale number there is permanent. That file is listed under never_touch — the bridge reports a mismatch via `doctor` (PI_CATALOG_CONTEXT_STALE) and deliberately does not rewrite it; see bridge/lib/pi-models.js for why.

managed.note: declared link: ~/.agents/skills is a link to ~/.claude/skills (a junction on Windows). pi's docs support ~/.agents/skills natively, so this path is shared rather than copied: changes in the source are visible immediately, nothing is duplicated, and there is no drift to reconcile. The bridge creates the link when it is missing, so a fresh machine needs no manual ln -s. If you would rather the bridge own a real copy, change mode to copy-tree (remove the link first — the planner refuses to write through one).
pi exposes prompt templates as /<filename> commands
home-level context file; avoids a second copy under .pi/agent that pi would also load

pi >= 1.4 reads ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json natively (user level; .pi/mcp.json is the project level), so the built-in MCP client is the transport and the pi-mcp-adapter package is no longer part of this target. The built-in client's default exposure is "codemode" — callable from codemode scripts but NOT declared to the model — so server_settings covers every derived server with exposure "direct" (the '*' entry) to keep the tool list the adapter used to provide (its `directTools: true`) and to keep the hard gate's mcp__<server>__<tool> names visible. A per-server entry can still override the wildcard. TWO THINGS THIS FILE CANNOT DO: it cannot enable built-in MCP (settings.json `extensions: ["-builtin:mcp"]` disables it) and it cannot uninstall a replacement extension (settings.json `packages: ["npm:pi-mcp-adapter"]` would supersede the built-in client, per docs/mcp.md: an installed extension registering /mcp replaces built-in MCP, and pi then does not read mcp.json at all). settings.json is never_touch on purpose, so `doctor` warns (MCP_SUPERSEDED) instead of rewriting it: the fix is the user removing those two entries.

mcp_supersede.note: pi supersedes the built-in MCP client in two independent ways: settings.json `extensions` may contain "-builtin:mcp" (built-in support disabled), and an installed extension that registers /mcp - pi-mcp-adapter is the known one - replaces it outright, after which pi does not read mcp.json at all (docs/mcp.md). Either way the file this target generates is on disk, correct, and read by nobody, which is the failure this block lets `doctor` name. settings.json is never_touch, so the finding is a warn with the fix, never a rewrite.

gates.mount_hint: pi loads ~/.pi/agent/extensions/*.ts and subdirectories containing index.ts or index.js, so no manual mount is needed
